tier_reason: First-party table in benchmarks/README.md backed by public harness code (benchmarks/src/index.cpp, index.js, Perf.js) and stated emcc flags (benchmarks/package.json), but the Emscripten version is not stated and the CPU is given only as '2.4 GHz Intel Core i5' (MacBook Pro Late 2013) with no model number, so it falls short of A; no independent measurement, so C.

corrections.baseline: snabbdom 0.7.0 (JavaScript virtual DOM library, in-browser; version pinned in benchmarks/package.json)
corrections.claimed_speedup: README text says apps written with it 'will run until 4 times faster', a projection, not a measured row. Measured table (lower is better; units not stated on the page, but Perf.js times each run with performance.now(), so milliseconds per call of a 100-iteration loop): Firefox 67.0.1: create nodes 1.0 vs 0.0, diff equal nodes 2.0 vs 9.0, diff different nodes 20.0 vs 23.0, add/remove nodes 22.0 vs 25.0 (asm-dom vs snabbdom). Chrome 75.0.3770.80: create nodes 0.585 vs 0.455, diff equal nodes 2.395 vs 3.11, diff different nodes 17.795 vs 11.405, add/remove nodes 15.17 vs 15.63. Ratios (derived from page data): Chrome diff equal nodes 1.30x faster, add/remove 1.03x faster, diff different nodes 1.56x slower, create nodes 1.29x slower; Firefox diff equal nodes 4.5x faster, diff different nodes 1.15x faster, add/remove 1.14x faster, create nodes slower at timer resolution.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Emscripten emcc (version not stated), benchmarks/package.json compile:wasm: -O3 --bind --memory-init-file 0 --llvm-lto 3 --llvm-opts 3 --js-opts 1 --closure 1 -s MODULARIZE=1 -s ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1 -s AGGRESSIVE_VARIABLE_ELIMINATION=1 -s ABORTING_MALLOC=1 -s NO_EXIT_RUNTIME=1 -s NO_FILESYSTEM=1 -s DISABLE_EXCEPTION_CATCHING=2 -s BINARYEN=1 -s BINARYEN_TRAP_MODE='allow'; snabbdom 0.7.0 bundled with webpack 2.4.1 and babel 6.24.1.
corrections.caveats: Weak and mixed evidence: asm-dom is slower than snabbdom on two of four rows in Chrome (diff different nodes 1.56x slower, create nodes 1.29x slower, derived from page data) and on create nodes in Firefox. The '4 times faster' figure is a stated expectation for whole apps, not a benchmark result. Harness flaws seen in benchmarks/src/Perf.js: the 'median' of 10 runs uses Array.prototype.sort() with no comparator, which sorts the timings as strings, and then takes index ceil(10/2)=5, so the reported value is not a true median whenever runs straddle a power of ten (e.g. 9.x and 1x.x ms); runs reuse one setup and swap vnode pairs between iterations. asm-dom runs with config.unsafePatch=true and clearMemory=false and pre-grows its heap in main(), settings an app would not normally use. The create-nodes row for asm-dom includes deleteVNode while snabbdom leaves deletion to the garbage collector, and neither create test touches the DOM. Firefox values are whole numbers, consistent with Firefox's coarsened performance.now() resolution (inference), so the Firefox create row (1 vs 0) is at timer resolution. Units are not stated in the README (code shows milliseconds). Emscripten version unstated; CPU model number unstated; 2013 hardware and 2019 browsers; README typo 'snabbbom'. README badge marks the project 'experimental'. Last commit 2022-08-28, last version v0.7.0 (2020-08-16). Kept as a documented flagged entry, not as a clear win.

notes: Numbers in the record match benchmarks/README.md exactly; added derived ratios, the emcc flags from benchmarks/package.json, and harness flaws read from Perf.js (string-sorted 'median') and index.cpp (unsafePatch=true, clearMemory=false). MIT licence confirmed from LICENSE.md (with snabbdom portions credited); 2.8k stars, 87 forks, not archived on the page; last commit 2022-08-28 makes it abandoned. Shortcomings to record: mixed results (slower on 2 of 4 Chrome rows), mis-sorted median statistic, unstated Emscripten version and CPU model, abandoned since 2022.

tier_reason: The repository has no benchmark code or numbers; the README has only the qualitative statement that convolution and edge-detection filters 'will run very slowly or hang the browser completely without WebAssembly support', and test/test.js is a page-load smoke test. A press snippet quotes a developer figure (see notes) but the article could not be opened, so D stays.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Emscripten emcc (version not stated), cpp/compileWASM.sh: -lm -O3 -s WASM=1 -s BINARYEN_IMPRECISE=1 -s ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1
corrections.caveats: Tier D: no benchmark, no numbers, no hardware in the repository. Only the qualitative README statement above. A WebSearch snippet (snippet only; infoworld.com was unreachable) of an InfoWorld article by Paul Krill dated 2017-04-04 quotes co-developer Deep Pulusani: 'In our performance tests, which you can demo here, we were able to surpass JavaScript performance by at least 200 percent', with no workload, browser, hardware or method. The baseline is the package's own JS fallback, not an independent JS library and not a native build, and the README's TODO says the JS fallbacks for underground, rooster, mist, kaleidoscope, bacteria, hulk edge, ghost and twisted are not yet matched to their C++ counterparts, so those filters would not compute the same result. Built with -s BINARYEN_IMPRECISE=1 (imprecise float-to-int conversions). LICENSE file is MIT while package.json says ISC (both OSI). Last commit 2017-06-05, so abandoned; it targets the 2017 Emscripten/Binaryen toolchain. 1.5k stars, 112 forks.

notes: Confirmed as a notable D entry (1.5k stars); repository has no measurement. Possible lift to C only if the InfoWorld 2017-04-04 article can be opened to confirm the developer's 'at least 200 percent' claim (seen as a search snippet only). Shortcomings to record: no numbers, self-baseline JS fallback with 8 filters not matched to the C++ code, BINARYEN_IMPRECISE build, abandoned since 2017, MIT vs ISC licence mismatch in package.json.
